analysis.title: Stewart Information Services Corp (STC): Initiating coverage with a Neutral rating and $49 price target
key_insights: GS initiates STC at Neutral with a $49 12-month price target (~14% upside from $43.10). The target is 9x GS 2027E EPS of $5.50.
STC is the smallest of the four large US title insurers, with ~11% total premium share as of 1H26 (up ~100bps vs. 2019). FNF holds ~32%, FAF ~26% and ORI ~14%.

Management targets ~15% share in direct, 15-20% in national commercial and 15%+ in agency, all in 2028+. GS models ~13% in direct and ~13% in agency by 2028 and does not assume further large acquisitions.
GS estimates the market is pricing in ~13% direct share and ~12% agency share by 2028. Reaching the 15% goals would be ~13% upside to Street direct premiums and ~20% upside to Street agency premiums.

GS forecasts title revenue growth of +2.0% YoY in 2027 and ~7% in 2028. Existing home sales (EHS) are forecast at -0.4% in 2027, and consensus is ~3% for 2027 and 2.5% for 2028. Mortgage rates near 7% keep EHS subdued.

Fee per file has offset falling volume. Domestic orders are down ~11% since 2018 at STC while fee per file is up ~60%. GS expects residential fee per file growth to slow as home price appreciation fades.

The $30mn cost program announced in 4Q26 is expected to be realized in 2027. GS estimates it adds $0.75 to EPS and lifts title margin ~100bps to ~7% in 2027, in line with the Street. GS models ~8% in 2028 against consensus of ~7.3%.

STC's cost base is 20-30% true fixed, 30-40% variable and the remainder semi-variable. GS estimates incremental costs run at a ~51% beta to revenue. Headcount rose to 8,400 in 3Q26 from 7,800 at YE25.

Mortgage rate sensitivity: at ~7% mortgage rates GS estimates the title market is ~6% below 1H26 annualized. At 7.5-8.0% it falls by a mid-teens percentage, and at 6.5% it grows ~8%. Historically a ~100bps decline in rates is needed to move EHS meaningfully.

Commercial title has been a growth tailwind, with fee per file up from $12.2k in 2023 to $17.8k in 2026E, partly from data center and energy deals. GS is cautious on its pace because of AI capex return concerns and possible legislation after Democrats regained control of Congress.
GS estimates commercial contributes ~70% of total title revenue growth in 2027E, up from 18% in 2026E. It estimates commercial fee per file falls ~5% in 2027 from the 4Q26 base.

Regulatory overhang: the FHFA title insurance pilot waives the lender's title policy on eligible Fannie Mae refinance loans. FHFA is due to publish nationwide rollout updates in early December 2026. Refinance is only ~6% of STC direct revenue vs. ~10% at peers, so GS sees STC as less exposed than peers.

State rate regulation: promulgated-rate states (Texas, Florida, New Mexico) are ~21% of STC title revenue vs. ~26% at peers. Texas ordered a ~10% premium cut in 2025, later reduced to ~6.2%, which STC called a low-single-digit EPS impact in 2026.
Valuation: STC trades at ~8.2x consensus 2027 EPS, ~93% of peers (FAF and FNF) and below the ~11x historical title average. YTD consensus EPS revisions for 2027 are -22% for STC vs. -4% for peers.

Upside case: if STC reaches its share goals in a stable market with a ~10% margin, GS sees EPS of $10+ vs. $5.50 for 2027E. With a 12% margin in a 5mn EHS market, GS sees $13+. These cases imply 3-4x EPS.

Acquisition math: STC cites $200-300mn of direct acquisitions at 4-6x EBITDA. GS estimates this adds ~$350mn of revenue and ~$50mn of EBITDA (17% of consensus 2028E). It notes a possible equity raise, as in 2025.
Real Estate Solutions revenue grew from ~$40mn in 2019 to a ~$785mn run-rate in 3Q26 via acquisitions (Propstream, Informative Research, MCS). STC guides to a 13-14% pre-tax margin in 2027.

market_movers.rationale: Share gains and cost saves support EPS growth, but a weak mortgage market slows margin expansion. At ~8.2x 2027 EPS the risk/reward is balanced with upside skew if rates fall.

sector_views.rationale: Volumes depend on existing home sales and mortgage rates near 7%. Peers trade at 8.2-12.6x 2027E EPS, with regulatory overhang from the FHFA pilot and state rate setting.

earnings_insights: GS estimates (not reported figures): STC EPS of $4.55 for 2026E, $5.50 for 2027E and $6.80 for 2028E. The cover table shows 12/25 EPS of $4.89, while GS's diluted pre-exceptional EPS line shows $4.05 for 2025.
Consensus EPS (FactSet) is $4.98 for 2026E, $5.29 for 2027E and $5.42 for 2028E. GS is below consensus in 2026E and above it in 2027E and 2028E.
GS forecasts total revenue of $3,438.8mn for 2026E, $3,570.0mn for 2027E and $3,800.3mn for 2028E, with net income of $107.9mn, $147.4mn and $189.5mn.
GS forecasts core organic title pre-tax margin of 6.0% for 2026E, 7.0% for 2027E and 8.0% for 2028E. Implied consensus core title margins are 6.5%, 7.0% and 7.3%.
STC's 3Q26 pre-tax title margin was 6.1% on an adjusted basis, vs. 17.1% at FNF, 12.7% at FAF and 6.7% at ORI (reported).
STC's 3Q26 commercial fee per file was $16.3k, with some deals pushed to 4Q.
Management's guidance points to a double-digit pre-tax margin exiting 2028, and GS models ~10% 4Q28E exit margins.
STC management says the $30mn cost program should support a ~15% EPS increase in 2027 vs. 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Elevated rates keep existing home sales subdued and pressure title premium growth and margin expansion.
Flat-to-down volumes in 2027 mean STC growth relies on share gains, pricing and cost cuts.
Slowing price growth reduces the pricing tailwind to STC's fee per file.
Down from $2.10tr in 2026E, which limits title volume growth.

risk_factors: Slower-than-expected margin expansion from weaker revenue growth.
Slowing commercial title growth, especially data center and energy deals, which would pressure 2027 revenue growth.
Regulatory risk from the FHFA title insurance pilot, which could expand to purchase transactions, and from state rate cuts like Texas in 2025.
Possible equity raise tied to acquisition-led share gains, as in 2025.
Goldman Sachs disclosures list investment banking compensation, a client relationship, a 1%+ ownership position and market-making in STC.
geopolitical: With Democrats back in control of Congress, news reports point to legislative action aimed at consumer energy costs from the AI build-out and calls for data center moratoriums.
President Trump's executive order on housing costs directed FHFA to explore expanding the title insurance pilot to loans above 80% LTV and nationwide.

tension_points.bull_case: STC gains share in direct and agency, cost saves lift 2027 margin to ~7%, and a market recovery in 2028 supports ~8% margins and EPS of $6.80. GS sees $10+ EPS if share goals are reached. The shares trade at ~8.2x vs. a ~11x history.
tension_points.bear_case: Mortgage rates near 7% keep existing home sales flat to down, which slows margin expansion. STC's smaller scale and recent investment make it more exposed than peers, and consensus 2027 EPS has been cut 22% YTD.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained mortgage rate decline of ~100bps would confirm the bull case. Existing home sales falling below GS's 2027 forecast of -0.4% or slower-than-expected margin expansion would break it.

tension_points.bull_case: Commercial fee per file rose from $12.2k in 2023 to $17.8k in 2026E, and commercial is ~70% of 2027E title revenue growth. STC has gained commercial share from 10% in 2019 to 14% in 2026 YTD.
tension_points.bear_case: Concerns over AI capex returns and potential legislation targeting data center energy costs could slow data center and energy deals, a headwind to top-line growth if residential stays weak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Commercial revenue growing slower than GS's ~7% for 2027E would undermine the revenue outlook.
